newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds rebound with U.S. Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds rebound with U.S. Treasuries.

text.p: Argentine bonds were mostly higher late Wednesday as the market turned around early declines in tandem with U.S. Treasuries.
"There was a rebound in U.S. Treasuries," said a trader at a large foreign bank and that helped the Argentine market. Still, activity remained slim through the session.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.10 to 120.60, while Argentina's FRB due 2005 fell 1/8 to 84-1/2.
Peso bonds did well again, with the peso-denominated Bocon Proveedor 1 due 2007 up 45 centavos to 92.70.
Another trader noted there was "a lack of clients" in the market.

Apart from the rebound in U.S. Treasuries during the session, the first trader said the release of strong industrial production figures Wednesday supported the market as "they confirmed the growth in the economy."
The independent FIEL consultants said October industrial production rose 11.7 percent from the same month a year earlier. Production rose 4.6 percent from a month earlier.
In the money markets, call money was unchanged at 6.15 percent.
